tonight.headline: 0–4, and 28 points short as the lineup stands
body: Bad news first. You lost Week 4 by 63.7 to 78.2 and are 0–4. For Week 5 your starting nine still holds Saquon Barkley at 0.0, Rashee Rice on bye and a tight end on bye, so ESPN projects you at 78.2 against 123.4 and gives you 26%.

Most of that gap closes today. Two swaps add 27.5 points and cost nothing, and a free tight end after 01:00 on Wednesday adds about ten more. That gets you to roughly 117 against a team whose own lineup has a hole at defence and two questionable starters.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Nacua 21.7, Goff 18.5, Kyren Williams 17.9, Jeremiyah Love 15.1 with a new ankle 'tweak', Tee Higgins 14.3 with a groin injury and 'day-to-day', Kittle 13.7. Their defence is Kansas City's, on bye at 0.0.

case.label: Your side once it is set
case.body: Taylor 19.0, Lawrence 18.1, Wilson 14.6, Tuten 14.0, Tate 13.5, Golden 12.8, a tight end near 10, Myers 8.8 and a defence between 5.6 and 7.7.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley practising in full, on your side. Love or Higgins sitting, on theirs.

doFirst.title: Bench Barkley, start Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: ESPN projects Barkley at 0.0 and Tuten at 14.0. Yesterday this was a fallback waiting for a ruling; the projection has now made it the lineup.

case.label: The injury
case.body: Right hamstring, four snaps in on Sunday. 'Week-to-week' and 'not considered a long-term issue' (NFL.com, Rapoport and Garafolo, Monday night). The Liberty Line on Tuesday: 'unlikely to play against Jaguars per source'. Pro Football Rumors' headline: 'Likely To Miss Week 5'. Nick Sirianni: 'more answers for you probably Wednesday'. He is not ruled out.

case.label: Why now and not Wednesday
case.body: Because the number already says so. This is the projection lineup, not an override of it, and both men play in the same game at 07:30 on Sunday, the earliest kickoff of the week. If you leave it for a ruling and forget, the slot scores zero.

case.label: Why Tuten
case.body: 17 of Jacksonville's 23 backfield carries on Sunday, 36 snaps to Chris Rodriguez's 15, and two touchdowns called back for holding (archive; NBC Sports, 4 Oct). He projects 14.0 against Gordon's 11.0 and Kamara's 10.0, so this is three points clear and not a coin flip. His brief exit on Sunday has no follow-up.

case.label: The other side of the same game
case.body: Tank Bigsby is going on injured reserve, so Will Shipley is Philadelphia's only healthy back. If Barkley does dress he does it at less than full health, against the defence ranked 2nd against running backs, with nobody to share the load.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Barkley plays on Sunday and outscores Tuten (archive).

doFirst.title: Rice is on bye: start Tate in his slot
doFirst.subtitle: Kansas City don't play. Tate projects 13.5, the highest of your three bench receivers, and has drawn more targets every week.

case.label: The slot
case.body: Rice projects 0.0 because the Chiefs are off, whatever his hamstring turns out to be. Tate is 13.5, Golden 12.8, Downs 12.1. The projection lineup is Wilson and Tate at receiver with Golden in the flex.

case.label: Tate
case.body: 9 catches on 12 targets for 145 on Sunday, and 6, 5, 9, 12 targets across four games with no injured teammate behind the rise (archive; A to Z Sports, 5 Oct). Cam Ward is healthy. Houston have allowed the second-most points to receivers in standard scoring, though the game has the week's lowest total at 39.5.

case.label: The flex is a coin flip
case.body: Downs is in your flex at 12.1 and the projection prefers Golden at 12.8. That is 0.7, inside the two-point line, so take Golden and write nothing down. Golden played 53 of 60 snaps and Jayden Reed's season is over; Downs drew 4 targets in London and Keenan Allen's status is unknown.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: For Tate, nothing can: Rice scores zero. Among Tate, Golden and Downs the gaps are 0.7 each, which is the projection's coin flip and not a call of mine.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Not before Wed 01:00 · then before Sunday
doFirst.title: After waivers clear, add a tight end for Waller
doFirst.subtitle: Your tight-end slot projects 0.0. Don't claim: wait until 01:00 Wednesday and add the best of Andrews, Strange, Loveland or Hockenson still there, free.

case.label: The hole
case.body: Waller is on bye and he is your only tight end. Four on the wire project between 9.6 and 10.4: Mark Andrews 10.4, T.J. Hockenson 10.1, Brenton Strange 9.7, Colston Loveland 9.6. All four are on waivers until Wed 7 Oct at 01:00 Mexico City.

case.label: Why not a claim
case.body: The four are 0.8 apart, which is a coin flip between any two of them, and a claim costs your place in an order that never resets. In a ten-team league at least one will clear. Not before Wed 7 Oct, 01:00 Mexico City: until then an add is a waiver claim, and a claim drops you from 8th to last in an order that never resets.

case.label: The order
case.body: Andrews first on the projection: 6, 7, 5, 6 targets, the steadiest of the four. His number assumes Lamar Jackson plays; Jackson left Sunday in a walking boot, his coach says 'I don't know the chances yet', and the line has moved from −6 to −3.5 (The Banner; SI, 5 Oct). If Jackson is ruled out before you add, skip him. Then Strange (8 targets and 95 yards on Sunday, Lawrence healthy, but Philadelphia allow the fewest points to tight ends), then Loveland (9 targets from Tyson Bagent, who is confirmed to start). Hockenson is last despite 10.1: his 13 targets came with Jefferson out, Jefferson may play, and Minnesota are off in Week 6, which would empty the slot again.

case.label: The drop, and the rule it bends
case.body: Waller. Neither clause of his open thesis has tripped, and you added him three days ago, so both the thesis rule and the churn rule say leave him. This is the exception and I am saying so: Wilson, Downs, Kamara, Gordon, Barkley and Rice each have an injured teammate and can't be named, the other seats are starters, and a tight end on bye is a slot at zero. ESPN's season number has Waller at 91.9 against 139.1, 127.9 and 121.0 for the first three, and his 8- and 6-target games were the two Coker didn't finish. Coker is expected back in Week 6.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The tight end you add scores less on Sunday than another of the four who was still free when you added (archive). For the drop: Waller outscores him in two of Weeks 6 to 8.

doFirst.title: Swap the Ravens' defence for the Jaguars', free
doFirst.subtitle: 5.6 against 7.7. Baltimore go to an Atlanta team that has scored 80 in two games; Jacksonville get an Eagles offence missing most of its backfield.

case.label: The gap
case.body: The Ravens project 5.6, the lowest number in your lineup. Free defences: Commanders 7.9, Jaguars 7.7, Steelers 7.4. Two points is outside the coin-flip line, which is the bar the strategy sets for a streaming move.

case.label: Why Jacksonville and not Washington
case.body: Philadelphia threw for 93 yards on Sunday and were sacked four times. Since then Bigsby has gone to injured reserve, Barkley is reported unlikely, DeVonta Smith is 'out indefinitely', Dallas Goedert is listed out, Landon Dickerson is on injured reserve and Cam Jurgens is in the concussion protocol (NBC Sports Philadelphia; The Liberty Line, 6 Oct). Jacksonville are 4.5-point favourites and PFN and Sportsnaut both rank them 5th for the week. The Commanders' 0.2 edge rests on one ranking (DraftSharks 5th; PFN has them 23rd).

case.label: Baltimore's side
case.body: 26.0 points a game allowed through Week 3; Marlon Humphrey hurt a calf on Sunday and Trey Hendrickson didn't play (The Banner; Yahoo; Football Nation USA). Atlanta scored 45 on Monday with 205 rushing yards. Dropping an 89%-owned defence needs a reason on the record, and that is it: the market is paying for the name.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: DraftSharks ranks the Jaguars 22nd this week, against the two 5ths. You changed defences on 30 Sep, so wait until Wednesday mid-morning and the seat is seven days old. Jacksonville are off in Week 7. Not before Wed 7 Oct, 01:00 Mexico City: until then an add is a waiver claim, and a claim drops you from 8th to last in an order that never resets.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The Ravens outscore the Jaguars on Sunday (archive), or Barkley and Smith both play.

whatWentWrong.title: As set, the lineup is 28.2 points short before anyone plays
whatWentWrong.lead: Barkley at 0.0, Rice on bye and a tight end on bye are all still in your starting nine. ESPN gives you 26% as it stands.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: lineup_check.py: 78.2 as set, 106.4 for the projection lineup, with the tight-end slot still at zero inside that. Kings of the North project 123.4. Setting the two swaps and adding a tight end takes you to about 117.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The first three cards. None of them is a judgement call: two players can't or probably won't play and one position is empty. Week 4 was lost 63.7 to 78.2 with 61.7 points on the bench, and most of that was two injury exits nobody could have set a lineup around. This week's zeros are known on Tuesday.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley practising in full and ESPN restoring his projection above Tuten's. Thursday's brief checks.

whatWentWrong.sources: lineup_check.py · ESPN league file · Week 4 archive

whatWentWrong.title: Barkley is 'week-to-week', and the man behind him is on injured reserve
whatWentWrong.lead: Monday night's reports rule out anything long-term and stop short of ruling him in for London.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: NFL.com: week-to-week, London 'remains uncertain'. The Liberty Line: unlikely. NBC's summary of Rapoport: 'expected to miss multiple games'. Bigsby had core-muscle surgery and misses at least four games. Philadelphia's offence has also lost DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert for now.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The first card, and the reasoning in the fourth: the same injury list is why Jacksonville's defence is the stream. It doesn't make Will Shipley an add. You own three backs who project above his 7.8.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A ruling on Wednesday that Barkley misses more than London. Then Shipley, a free agent after 01:00, is worth Kamara's place in the queue, though not Kamara's seat while Etienne is out.

whatWentWrong.sources: NFL.com · The Liberty Line · NBC Sports · PFT

whatWentWrong.title: The Waller add left one tight end and no cover for his bye
whatWentWrong.lead: You added him on 3 Oct, the day before his last game before a bye. He scored 6.6 and now the slot is empty.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Archive: Waller 6.6 on 6 targets with Coker inactive; Sadiq, the tight end you dropped, 0.0. Your move won that week. The seat has changed hands four times in about two weeks, and the third card would make it five.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The third card names Waller as the drop and says plainly that it bends two rules to do it. The alternative is a zero at tight end in a week ESPN has you at 26%.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: You preferring to keep Waller and drop a back instead. The screen protects Kamara and Gordon because Etienne and Achane are out; I have followed it.

case.body: Wednesday after 01:00 Mexico City, free, if Andrews has been claimed or Lamar Jackson has been ruled out.

worthALook.name: Colston Loveland
worthALook.lead: Carried from yesterday: his condition is met, and he is third in the queue.

case.label: The role
case.body: 6 catches on a team-high 9 targets for 57 from Tyson Bagent: 11.7 (archive). Targets 2, 3, 4, 9. Bagent starts again at Green Bay: 'Tyson will be the guy' (Ben Johnson, 5 Oct). Green Bay are without Micah Parsons and lost Edgerrin Cooper for the season.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: One game of volume and no column mentions him. He is 91.4% owned, the least likely of the four to clear, and you dropped him on 25 Sep at 3 and 4 targets.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Wednesday after 01:00, free, if Andrews and Strange are both gone.

worthALook.sources: Week 1–4 archive · NBC Sports · NFL.com · packers.com

worthALook.name: T.J. Hockenson
worthALook.lead: Carried from yesterday. Thirteen catches, and last in the queue for two reasons.

case.label: The role
case.body: 13 catches on 13 targets for 119, a 40% share, after 13 targets in the three games before (vikings.com; SI, 5 Oct). SI: 'So long as Jefferson is out... Hockenson is a shoo-in top-10 tight end.' New Orleans are 22nd against tight ends.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: It depends on Justin Jefferson, whose coach has 'no real projection' and who is trying to practise this week. And Minnesota are off in Week 6, so dropping Waller for him empties the slot again in five days. RotoWire and NFL.com both name him, so he is the likeliest to be claimed.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Only if Jefferson is ruled out before you add and the other three are gone.

worthALook.sources: Week 1–4 archive · vikings.com · SI · NFL.com · RotoWire

worthALook.name: Will Shipley
worthALook.lead: The handcuff to your Barkley and every column's top pickup. Not an add while you own three backs above him.

case.label: The role
case.body: The only healthy back on Philadelphia's roster after Bigsby's surgery (NFL.com; PFT, 5 Oct). 6 carries for 23 on 29 snaps on Sunday. Yahoo and RotoWire lead their columns with him.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He projects 7.8 against Tuten's 14.0, Gordon's 11.0 and Kamara's 10.0, faces the 2nd-ranked run defence, and Philadelphia threw for 93 yards. A claim would cost your priority for a sixth back.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley ruled out beyond London on Wednesday. He is a free agent after 01:00 if nobody claims him, which at 0.7% owned here is possible.

worthALook.sources: NFL.com · PFT · Yahoo · RotoWire · Week 4 archive

doNotChase.name: Joe Mixon
doNotChase.lead: The wire's biggest riser, +6.51. He signed, but to a practice squad.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Seattle signed him to the practice squad on Monday, pending a physical (PFT/NBC Sports; DraftSharks, 5 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He hasn't played since January 2025 and needs an elevation to dress. Emanuel Wilson had 21 carries on Sunday and Zach Charbonnet's practice window is open. No projection.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: An elevation to the 53 and a coach describing a role.

doNotChase.name: Tyreek Hill
doNotChase.lead: Carried, and it touches your own receiver: Kansas City have called his agent.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Tyquan Thornton needs ankle surgery and is out three to four months, Rice is hurt, and the Chiefs have contacted Hill's agent (CBS, citing The Athletic, 4–5 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: No signing, a knee dislocation from September 2025, and 'ready by November' is his agent's word. If Kansas City did sign him, the targets he took would be Rice's.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A signing, then a practice.

doNotChase.sources: CBS Sports · AP · ESPN league file

doNotChase.name: Tyler Shough
doNotChase.lead: Carried from yesterday's watch list, and closed: he projects 3.5 under Lawrence.

case.label: The rise
case.body: An 87%-owned quarterback sitting on your wire, with the league lead in dropbacks.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 14.6 against Lawrence's 18.1. Monday: 30 of 48 for 286 with one late touchdown, his first week outside the top twelve (DraftSharks), a swollen left hand (Heavy), and Minnesota's defence next.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A week in which he projects two or more above Lawrence. This isn't it.

doNotChase.name: Malik Washington
doNotChase.lead: Carried: Yahoo's receiver add of the week, in an offence that threw for 85 yards.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 5 catches on 5 targets for 67, 12.0 (archive); target shares of 28% and 29% (Yahoo, 5 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Targets 8, 5, 10, 5 from a quarterback who was 9 of 17. He would be your sixth receiver and a claim costs priority.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets against Cincinnati, or a different quarterback in Miami.

doNotChase.name: Makai Lemon
doNotChase.lead: Carried: six targets with Smith out, and the columns prefer a different Eagle.

case.label: The rise
case.body: DeVonta Smith is 'out indefinitely' (NBC Sports Philadelphia, 6 Oct). Lemon played 45 snaps.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 3 catches on 6 targets for 27, 5.7 (archive). Darius Cooper played 55 snaps and caught both touchdowns.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets in London.

doNotChase.sources: Week 4 archive · NBC Sports Philadelphia · RotoWire

doNotChase.name: Dontayvion Wicks
doNotChase.lead: Carried: Philadelphia's most-used receiver by snaps, and quiet three weeks running.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 56 snaps, 92%, with Smith out (NBC Sports Philadelphia, 5 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 3 catches for 18 on 5 targets, after 5.2 the week before (archive). Hurts threw for 93 yards. Below all four of your healthy receivers.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets in London.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Eleven names clear the tool's bar, and at running back and receiver the bar is an artefact: it measures them against Barkley and Rice, whose last week was an injury exit each. Four weeks of data. The only question research turns into a move is at tight end, where the tool doesn't see that Waller is on bye; that is the third card.

rising.name: Keaton Mitchell
rising.roleReason: A three-man committee by design with Omarion Hampton healthy: snaps 26, 25, 25 on Sunday, and he is 'a favorite of OC Mike McDaniel' (Yahoo, 5 Oct). Volume, 10 carries and 6 targets, without a lead role. He isn't on the published wire.
rising.action: WATCH — a committee third; the trigger is Hampton missing a game

rising.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
rising.roleReason: Bijan Robinson is healthy and ran 19 times for 145. Brian Robinson's three touchdowns came from 4, 8 and 11 yards in a 45–24 blowout as the short-yardage back (PFF; NFL.com, 5 Oct).
rising.action: WATCH — touchdowns and game script behind a healthy starter

rising.name: MarShawn Lloyd
rising.roleReason: Green Bay's lead back by snaps, 33 of 60, while Josh Jacobs is on the exempt list: 7 carries for 13 and 5 catches, with a fumble. Kaleb Johnson ran better and fumbled at the goal line (Yahoo, 5 Oct). You dropped him for Gordon.
rising.action: WATCH — volume at 1.9 yards a carry in a backfield nobody has won

rising.name: Mike Washington Jr.
rising.roleReason: Ashton Jeanty's handcuff; Jeanty played 67% of the snaps (DraftSharks). 9 carries for 18.
rising.action: WATCH — nothing unless Jeanty is hurt

rising.name: Romeo Doubs
rising.roleReason: 9 targets and two touchdowns against Buffalo, longest catch 15 yards (DraftSharks). A.J. Brown, now a Patriot, is on injured reserve and hoped back by Week 6.
rising.action: WATCH — one nine-target game, with the team's best receiver due back

rising.name: Devaughn Vele
rising.roleReason: 66 snaps, 89%, the most of any Saints skill player (Athlon). On Monday 5 of his 6 catches and the touchdown came after half-time in a 45–24 loss (DraftSharks, 6 Oct). Jordyn Tyson isn't expected back before Week 7. The steadiest role on this list.
rising.action: WATCH — a real role; a claim would spend priority on a sixth receiver

rising.name: Khalil Shakir
rising.roleReason: 7 catches on 8 targets for 82, his best game; DJ Moore aggravated a shoulder injury and is uncertain for Monday night (RotoWire, 5 Oct).

rising.name: Tyquan Thornton
rising.roleReason: Dislocated his left ankle on Sunday after 5 catches for 111 and two touchdowns; surgery, three to four months (CBS, 5 Oct).
rising.action: WATCH — off the list: out until at least January

rising.name: T.J. Hockenson
rising.roleReason: A 40% target share with Jefferson out and Murray throwing checkdowns at 6.7 yards a completion (SI, 5 Oct). Jefferson is trying to practise this week, and Minnesota are off in Week 6.
rising.action: WATCH — last of the four tight ends for Waller's slot; see the card

rising.name: Michael Mayer
rising.roleReason: 10 targets beside a healthy Brock Bowers, who had 11, because Kirk Cousins threw 52 times and Nailor left with a concussion (DraftSharks; PlayerProfiler). A second tight end whose volume is pass volume. New England, next, allow the fewest points to tight ends.
rising.action: WATCH — behind the four in the card

rising.name: Brenton Strange
rising.roleReason: 8 targets, 95 yards and a 35% share with no injury behind it (NBC Sports, 4 Oct). Targets have gone 3, 2, 5, 8.
rising.action: ADD — if he is the best of the four tight ends left after waivers clear; second in the card's order

settled.title: Week 4 final: 63.7 to 78.2
settled.result: Kyle Pitts added 7.7 for Team 13 on Monday (archive). You lost by 14.5. Kamara 22.8, Tate 21.5, Gordon 18.0 and Golden 11.7 on the bench would have scored 61.7 more than the four slots they could have filled. Barkley and Rice were injury exits; the rest was the projection's lineup.

settled.title: Downs in the flex (the projection lineup, 13.6 to Tate's 11.9)
settled.result: Archive: Downs 4.6, Tate 21.5. A coin flip by projection with no thesis written, and it lost by 16.9.

settled.result: Never fired as written: he isn't ruled out. ESPN's 0.0 has replaced it with today's first card. Closed EXPIRED, not RIGHT.

'Darren Waller: do not chase' (Saturday's brief)
settled.result: You added him. Archive: Waller 6.6, Sadiq 0.0. Your move won the week; three days later his bye leaves the slot empty.

settled.result: Archive: 18.0 on the bench. The lean was mine and it is withdrawn. He projects 11.0 this week, on the bench again.

settled.result: Allen and Slayton were inactive and Downs drew 4 targets (archive). Closed WRONG.

settled.result: Closed WRONG on 30 Sep; 24.9 on Sunday (archive). He is last in today's queue for a different reason: a Week 6 bye.

cannotSee.label: Which tight ends will clear
cannotSee.body: Andrews, Hockenson, Strange and Loveland are all on waivers until Wed 7 Oct at 01:00 Mexico City. ESPN shows only your own claims, so I can't see who is ahead of you; you are 8th of ten. The card's order is the plan; who is left is Wednesday's fact.

cannotSee.label: Medical results
cannotSee.body: No scan result is public for Barkley, Rice or Lamar Jackson. Barkley's ruling is promised for Wednesday, after waivers process. Jackson's decides whether Andrews's 10.4 means anything.

cannotSee.label: The two rules the third card bends
cannotSee.body: Dropping Waller breaks the letter of the churn rule (his seat changed on 3 Oct) and of the open-thesis rule (neither clause has tripped). I read a bye at a one-man position as the same thing as a ruling-out for this week. That is my interpretation, not the runbook's words.

cannotSee.label: Whether the projection has Monday night
cannotSee.body: Kamara's 10.0 was published after his game. I can't see when ESPN last recomputed it, so 'priced' for Monday's news is an inference from the timestamp.

cannotSee.label: Matchup grades
cannotSee.body: Every tile comes from FootballDB's points allowed through Week 4, standard scoring and four games deep. DraftEdge, undated and full PPR, disagrees on Pittsburgh against receivers (8th or 16th), Cleveland against receivers (27th or 15th) and Cincinnati against backs (11th or 25th). Houston grade as the second-softest defence for receivers while two outlets ranked their D/ST near the top last week.

cannotSee.label: The Jaguars' defence
cannotSee.body: Two rankings have them 5th and one has them 22nd. The case rests on Philadelphia's injury list, and Barkley and Smith are not officially out.

cannotSee.label: The wire screen
cannotSee.body: Keaton Mitchell, Antonio Williams, Oronde Gadsden, Tyler Higbee and Tyquan Thornton aren't on the published wire, so their availability here is the screen's inference.

cannotSee.label: Sources that disagree
cannotSee.body: Barkley: 'uncertain' (NFL.com), 'unlikely' (The Liberty Line), 'multiple games' (NBC's summary of Rapoport). Rice: 'isn't considered serious' (AP) or 'several weeks' (Silver). Lamar Jackson: day-to-day (Rapoport) or week-to-week (Florio). The Eagles' practice squad has two running backs (Bleacher Report) or none (NFL.com's summary). Alec Pierce's earliest return is Week 6 by CBS and Week 7 by the four-game rule.

cannotSee.label: Reports I couldn't retrieve
cannotSee.body: ESPN pages returned empty, including its stories on Lamar Jackson, Kamara's knee and the Vikings' line. Hogs Haven, Bleeding Green Nation, Stampede Blue, Behind the Steel Curtain, Buffalo Rumblings, Acme Packing Company and the Star Tribune were blocked. RotoBaller gave navigation only and NBC Sports blurbs mostly a headline and one line. FantasyPros' and Sharp Football's defence-against-position tables did not render, so every matchup grade rests on FootballDB, which is standard scoring, with DraftEdge beside it. O'Connell's Monday press conference exists only as video. Pages were read through a summarising tool, so quotes are close but may not be exact.

cannotSee.label: The trade market
cannotSee.body: No trade this run. Barkley and Rice are undiagnosed and Team 13's Lamar Jackson is hurt; nothing can be priced.

cannotSee.label: Josh Jacobs
cannotSee.body: Nothing dated after 25 Sep was found: still on the commissioner's exempt list, with a four-to-six-game suspension floated (Fowler, 18 Sep). He missed Week 4 and projects 0.0.
